# --instructions--

Write a function `dedupe` that takes an array of strings (omit the argument label) and returns a new array with the duplicates removed and the remaining values in ascending order

# --before-seed--

```swift
// DO NOT EDIT FROM HERE
import Foundation

var _testCount = 0
var _testFailedCount = 0
func tryCatch(_ assertion: Bool) {
    _testCount += 1
    if !assertion {
        _testFailedCount += 1
        print("Test Case '--err-t\(_testCount)--' failed")
    }
}
// DO NOT EDIT UNTIL HERE
```

# --asserts--

`dedupe(["b", "a", "b", "c", "a"])` must return `["a", "b", "c"]`

```swift
tryCatch(dedupe(["b", "a", "b", "c", "a"]) == ["a", "b", "c"])
```

`dedupe(["x", "x", "x"])` must return `["x"]`

```swift
tryCatch(dedupe(["x", "x", "x"]) == ["x"])
```

`dedupe([])` must return an empty array

```swift
tryCatch(dedupe([]) == [])
```

The function must return an array of strings

```swift
tryCatch(type(of: dedupe(["a"])) == [String].self)
```

# --after-asserts--

```swift
print("Executed \(_testCount) tests, with \(_testFailedCount) failures")
```

# --solutions--

```swift
func dedupe(_ items: [String]) -> [String] {
    return Set(items).sorted()
}
```
